profile.headline: Embedded Linux Engineer II, FW an Inseego Company
profile.summary:
I am a Software Engineer with rich problem solving skills that have been applied to a vast range of problems. I have developed flight routing for fuel optimizations, created an image processing algorithm for cell counting as well as created a cross-platform mobile app for steel fabrication. I developed a real-time video streaming application using Objective-C and C++ which took an RTSP network feed (h264/AAC) and synchronized the video frames with EEG data. Most recently I am writing features for an embedded linux system used in a cellular router.

I have developed and maintained code using C, C++, Objective-C, C#, Javascript, Lex, Yacc, Java, Matlab, Mathematica, Assembly and Shell scripting (bash, grep, sed, awk, etc.). I worked with both the front end GUIs and created back end libraries and APIs. I have written multi-threaded code to run on supercomputers and I have written streamlined applications for a single core embedded linux system, I am familiar with refactoring and am comfortable with version control and working with a distributed team. I love automating redundant tasks and scripting my way through the mundane predictable stuff.

I have worked as a Project Manager and have pushed projects through from the first moments of brainstorming into requirements gathering, through both internal and external documentation and all the way to releasing to customers. I understand the Software life cycle and I'm happy working across departmental lines to move projects forward.

positions.title: Linux Software Engineer, II
positions.description:
Lead Engineer on Skyus-SC embedded applications programmed exclusively in C. 

Lead Engineer on Skyus-E, Linux based cellular router platform. Embedded applications programmed in C++. Utilized bash scripting and system configuration tools throughout the project.

Peripheral Engineer promoted to Lead Engineer on Skyus-X, Linux based cellular router platform. 

Automated the build/release process for Skyus-E and Skyus-X product line. 

Implemented 'ip passthrough' proxy arp routing implementation for a custom feature request. 

Lead third party Linux integration efforts working side-by-side with engineers from partner companies such as Meraki, Dell and Intel.

Continuously ensured documentation on all platforms was up-to-date, accessible by all engineers and covered the entire software development life cycle from the early decisions to distributing the release notes for the final build.

I had the privilege of  working with modem modules from Sierra Wireless and Telit. Both have presented their own unique integration issues which lead me to a better understanding of cellular connectivity.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Project manager for Net Station 5.1, 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 software releases. Responsibilities include feature specification, sprint planning, product demos, collaboration across departments, understanding regulatory requirements and risks as well as feature requests and how to balance the two. 

Lead developer and integrator of new network based video streaming using Axis cameras. I was in charge of the product starting with the task of finding the specific camera hardware to develop with, writing code to integrate the systems, to running tests to prove timing accuracy, meetings with our marketing department to ensure all promotional materials were accurate. I also engage our sales and support divisions prior to all releases to ensure a positive customer experience with every new version.

Implementation of a new integrated real time streaming video solution required hardware, software, network and integration knowledge. Utilizing Axis VAPIX API, knowledge of ntp and Linux OS allowed the integrated solution to achieve sub-second timing accuracy as well as complete in-app camera control and video recording capabilities synchronized with EEG acquisition.

positions.title: Computer Information Technology Faculty
positions.description:
As a part time faculty member of the CIT department, I was independently responsible for curriculum development and delivery of instructional material both online and in the classroom for a new Health Informatics course, Networking and Health Information Exchange. 

The goal of the Health Informatics course, Networking and Health Information Exchange, was to educate individuals to be effective developers, users and managers of health information resources.  More specifically I covered both the technical side of Networking as well as the current laws and best practices affecting the exchange of health information. We looked at computer networks and touched on vulnerabilities which affect the safety of handling health information, encryption strategies and security measures necessary for protecting sensitive information. 

While I taught the current best practices, my main goal was to teach my students how to find the current best practices from reliable sources to ensure they are able to keep up with the rapidly changing regulations and implementation standards in the future. 

Health Informatics is the study of how medical data is collected, stored and communicated; how the data is processed into health information suitable for administrative and clinical decision making; and how computer technology, communications technology, and other information management skills can be applied to support these processes.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Creating and maintaining programs to solve industrial-scale scheduling and routing problems using novel, AI-based approaches. 

Projects included adding features to an aircraft routing software package which touched all aspects of our product line including Windows (C#), centOS (C++, lex, yacc), database (SQL), product documentation, creating training materials and mentoring new employees.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
FabTrol Pro: Creating modules and new functionality in the FabTrol Pro steel fabrication management software using C#, SQL, Visual Studio and Subversion.

FabTrol Mobile: Project lead in development of a cross-platform mobile application as an extension of the FabTrol Pro product line. Cross platform functionality achieved using C# and SQL on the back-end and Ext JS, Javascript and Sencha Touch for the front end.

positions.title: Graduate Research Fellow
positions.description:
Creating tools for segmentation and geometric measurement derived from image analysis of the human placenta to aid in the quantification of features which are known to impact the health of the child. This work is done in collaboration with Matt Sottile, Ph.D. (University of Oregon) and Carolyn Salafia, M.D. (Placental Analytics, LLC).

"Unsupervised segmentation for inflammation detection in histopathology images" is a paper I wrote and published in the series Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer Verlag.  It covers a method I developed for unsupervised threshold selection and segmentation of inflammatory polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMLs).  The qualitative grading of inflammatory response has poor inter-rater reliability. The paper presents an automated quantitative approach which is reliable and reproducible.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description: C++ programming and translation of Matlab code for EEG data analysis utilizing frequency domain Fourier analysis and data clustering methods.

positions.title: Transfer Coordinator
positions.description:
•	Coordinated doctors, surgeons and other care providers for trauma and critically ill patients.
•	Responsible for transferring critical patients between hospitals and ensuring continuation of care.
•	Oversaw doctor to doctor communication and reporting to maintain compliance with Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act (EMTALA).

honors.title: Professional Distinctions
honors.description: Professional Distinctions is an honor awarded to University of Oregon students taking extra efforts to grow outside their core discipline. During my undergraduate studies, my core discipline was Mathematics and I received professional distinctions in Computer Science for my cross discipline work with the Neuroinformatics Center and the Computer Science department to port a mathematical algorithm from Matlab into C++ for a significant increase in performance when applied to EEG data.

volunteerExperiences.role: Mentor & Coach - Willamette High School Programming Club
volunteerExperiences.description: As a mentor and coach to the Willamette High School programming club I offered my time and troubleshooting skills to the students as they worked on developing programming and design skills to put together an original video game. They did everything from recording original music and drawing the original artwork to programming the logic. They utilized Unity (C#) to create a fun side-scrolling video game.

118 college students participated from 6 states (OR, WA, CA, CO, IN, MA), 14 universities and representing 16 different majors. Over 100+ high school students, community & business leaders engaged in our weekend-long event.

“The local Eugene-Springfield gaming community came out in force to help mentor and support our students all weekend long,” said co-organizer Kate Harmon, undergraduate program manager of the Lund­quist Center for Entrepreneurship. “This was a cross-disciplinary event that shows the power of working collaboratively together.” -- Register-Guard, JAN. 24, 2016
